curation.notes: Dual-trap optical tweezers with widefield fluorescence: single isolated human mitotic chromosomes (U2OS and HCT116, telomere-biotinylated via TRF1-BirA) held between two streptavidin beads and probed by stretch curves, oscillatory rheology, force clamp, polyamine/PEG/salt condensation and in situ high-salt histone depletion. Performed on both a LUMICKS C-Trap and a similarly equipped academic set-up.

evidence.snippet: Experiments were carried out at around 27 °C, slightly above room temperature.
Forces were determined using a position-sensitive detector and they were binned to match the frame rate used for distance detection (~20 Hz).
a 20 W trapping laser (1,064 nm; YLR-20-LP, IPG Photonics)

evidence.snippet: a 20 W trapping laser (1,064 nm; YLR-20-LP, IPG Photonics)
Trap stiffnesses were calibrated using the thermal noise method before each experiment and were usually around 0.5 pN nm−1.
All experiments were performed using streptavidin-coated polystyrene beads (4.47 or 4.88 μm diameter, Spherotech).
Stretch curves were recorded with a pulling velocity of 0.2 μm s−1 to a maximum force of between 250 and 350 pN.

entities.name: Mitotic chromosome (U2OS TRF1-BirA ± H2B-eGFP; HCT116 TOP2A-mAID H2B-eGFP CDK1as TRF1-BirA)

evidence.snippet: For most experiments, chromosomes were isolated from U2OS TRF1-BirA cells with or without H2B-eGFP as described previously22.
We combine these experiments with high-salt histone depletion and theory to show that chromosomal elasticity originates from the chromatin fibre behaving as a flexible polymer
